key_insight: MindView tests whether AI can generate spatially consistent views of a scene from partial multi-view observations and language instructions. It introduces a benchmark with 1,500 samples from 513 scenes across three indoor datasets.
problem_solved: Existing generative spatial evaluations leave language-guided view generation underexplored: can a model preserve a scene’s spatial structure when asked to show it from a different viewpoint?
method: Evaluate language-guided generation using partial multi-view observations of indoor scenes.
Organize seven tasks into two families; geometry-dominant tasks specify changes in camera position and orientation.
Use 1,500 samples covering 513 scenes from three indoor datasets. The provided abstract is truncated, so the second task family and evaluation details are not available.
impact: MindView offers practitioners a benchmark for assessing spatial consistency in generative models beyond image editing. It focuses attention on whether generated views reflect a coherent scene, not just plausible-looking images.

paper_title: MindView: Benchmarking Generative Multi-View Spatial Intelligence
paper_authors: Yanbo Wang, Siqi Luo, Siyu Zhang, Chenming Zhu, Wenzhao Zheng
